title: Onboarding region activation: legal timeline and operator scripts
summary: A pragmatic runbook for activating a customer's regional tenancy (region activation) that stitches together legal gating, operator steps, telemetry checks, and evidence packaging for audits. Focused on the activation window, canary progress, and a fast kill-switch + rollback path.
purpose: Provide a single, operator-friendly document that product, SRE, legal, and CS can use when turning on region-specific hosting for a customer. Clarifies ownership at each step, what evidence must be produced, and how to handle exceptions during activation.
scope: Applies to Private and Dedicated customers requesting region-specific activation (customer requests to host data wholly within a named territory). Covers pre-activation gating, activation weekend procedure, post-activation evidence delivery, and emergency rollback. Does NOT cover long-term migration orchestration or billing change details.
prerequisites: 1) Signed region addendum from Legal and Sales (scan stored in customer folder). 2) Tenant metadata set with 'region_activated: false' and 'region_requested' populated. 3) Capacity reservation confirmed in Regional Pool (ops ticket ENG-4218). 4) Target infra image version and config hash pinned (ops-configs PR referenced). 5) Customer acceptance test (CAT) checklist has owner assigned in CS-2987.
activation_timeline: T-7 to T-2: Legal signoff and jurisdictional checklist completed; place customer in 'staged' cohort and create activation Jira. T-1: Smoke tests queued in staging region; SRE run through operator checklist; customer notified of 1-hour maintenance window. Day 0 (activation): 00:00 start window; perform canary at 5% traffic for 30m; verify telemetry; increase to 25% for 45m; if healthy proceed to 100% ramp over 2 hours. Post-activation (Day 0+1): full evidence export and snapshot attached to customer audit bundle. Day 7: follow-up CAT and legal confirmation. All steps recorded in activation ticket.
operator_checklist: 1) Confirm legal artifact present and attached to ticket. 2) Verify region tag on tenant metadata (region_requested matches capacity region). 3) Reserve capacity slot in regional pool and annotate with activation window. 4) Create canary route and apply traffic-split config (5% initial). 5) Kick off preflight smoke suite (connectivity, KMS reachable, egress filter rules). 6) Observe token-level latency and error-rate dashboards for calced SLOs. 7) After 30m and green metrics, raise to 25% and repeat checks. 8) If any metric breach > threshold, run kill-switch (see section). 9) When at 100%, flip tenant region_activated:true, tag release_hash in ticket, and notify CS/Legal. 10) Trigger evidence export job and attach artifacts to ticket.
evidence_packaging_steps: 1) Generate routing proof: routing logs that show all region-bound requests matched regional endpoints for the activation window. 2) KV-anchor snapshot: export a timestamped snapshot showing tenant KV anchor location. 3) KMS access log extract: filtered by tenant key ID for the activation window. 4) Config manifest: ops-configs commit + applied config id. 5) Signed legal affirmation email (PDF). 6) Compose audit bundle zip and upload to encrypted customer folder; note location in ticket and send secure link to Legal/CS.
rollback_and_kill_switch: Kill-switch semantics: immediate and reversible. When triggered, traffic to the newly activated region must be diverted to the pre-activation routing (global fallback pool) and tenant metadata must be reverted to 'region_activated:false'. Steps: 1) Set routing override flag in deployment gateway (ops flag). 2) Disable regional DNS entries (if applicable) to prevent new binds. 3) Rollback config in regional pool to last-known-good commit. 4) Re-run cross-checks to ensure no writes occurred to region storage during window; if writes exist, escalate to Legal and Data-Integrity for quarantine. 5) Open incident and notify customer with templated comms. Important: keep kill-switch manual for first 72 hours post-activation for any high-risk customers.
telemetry_verification: Key checks during canary and ramp: - Error rate (5xx) vs baseline <= 2x - Latency p95 within 1.5x baseline - Token consumption delta explained by traffic split - KV cache miss rate acceptable (<5%) - Routing deviations: 0 mismatches allowed for pinned tenants. Use 'region-activation' dashboard and CLI quick-check script (ops/region_check.sh) to collect a 15m window sample. Collect screenshots and export CSVs to ticket.
escalation_and_legal_handoff: If evidence shows cross-border leakage or config mismatch: 1) Immediately notify Legal and Security with the audit bundle. 2) Legal to determine customer notification obligations and whether to engage regulators. 3) Security to produce forensic snapshot (immutable) and recommend quarantine timeframe. 4) CS to prepare customer-facing messaging with legal-approved wording. Escalation levels: L1 (operator action + ticket), L2 (Security + Legal review within 4 hours), L3 (exec escalation and regulator contact; target <24 hours for decision).
customer_comm_templates:
Pre-activation notice: 'We will begin activation of region X for your tenant during the timeframe YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM - HH:MM UTC. Expected downtime: none; brief maintenance window for network routing. Please ensure any time-sensitive operations are paused.'
Post-activation success: 'Region activation complete. Attached: audit bundle link and acceptance checklist. If you see any anomalies please notify your CSM.'
Rollback notice: 'We paused region activation due to operational anomalies. We reverted routing and are investigating; next update in 2 hours.'
open_questions: 1) Should kill-switch be automated for customers with SLAs > 99.9%? (cost vs safety tradeoff) 2) Do we require KMS key escrow for EU customers before activation or is proof of KMS connectivity sufficient? 3) How long should we retain activation audit bundles internally (default 90d?) 4) Who signs off when legal opinion contains conditional language? (default: Legal + Head of Security)
